/about-me/: I have been working as a Speech & Language Therapist since 2014, supporting children with a wide range of communication and developmental needs. Over the years, my clinical experience has shaped a strong focus on early intervention, alongside experience with children with neurological, genetic, and developmental conditions.
My clinical and academic experience has shaped the way I look at communication, not as one isolated skill, but as something connected to a child's development, relationships, and everyday life.

Continued professional development is an important part of my work. I have pursued specialized training in Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Interventions (NDBIs) and parent-mediated interventions, including approaches that support the development of social communication and interaction skills and approaches that help parents understand and respond to challenging behavior. I have also pursued specialized training in autism assessment, including the ADOS-2.

I am currently undertaking advanced training in behavior analysis as part of my professional development toward becoming an International Behavior Analyst (IBA). This ongoing training broadens my understanding of learning, motivation, communication, and behavior.
My behavior-analytic work is undertaken under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA), as appropriate to the work and the child's needs.

Alongside my clinical work, I am an academic coordinator and instructor at the Higher Institute of Speech and Language Therapy at Saint Joseph University of Beirut. I have been teaching and supervising students since 2018 and have served as academic coordinator since 2021.

My teaching and supervision include language and communication disorders, communication profiles associated with neurological and developmental conditions, and clinical decision-making. This academic role keeps me closely connected to current knowledge while bringing together the clinical and academic perspectives that shape my work.

At the heart of my work is the belief that every child has their own strengths, ways of learning, and ways of connecting with others. I also believe that parents are an important part of the process. They know their child best, and supporting communication means creating strategies that can become part of the child's real everyday life, within the relationships and routines that matter most.
/areas-of-expertise/: Early Communication & Language: Assessment and Intervention

I support young children with communication and language difficulties through assessment and individualized intervention, particularly during the early years. My work is guided by evidence-based practice and draws on complementary cognitive, developmental, and behavioral perspectives to understand each child's profile and identify meaningful goals.
Assessment

Assessment aims to build a comprehensive understanding of a child's communication and language abilities, strengths, needs, and everyday functioning. Depending on the child's profile and the questions being explored, I use standardized assessments alongside functional and dynamic assessment approaches.
Functional assessment tools, such as the VB-MAPP, may also be used when appropriate to help identify current skills, learning needs, and intervention priorities.
Early Communication & Language Intervention

Intervention is individualized to the child's communication profile, developmental level, interests, strengths, and family priorities. I draw primarily on principles from Naturalistic Developmental Behavioral Interventions (NDBIs) and parent-mediated interventions, integrating learning opportunities into play, everyday interactions, and familiar routines.
This work may support children with communication and language delays, autism, neurological conditions, genetic syndromes, and other developmental conditions.
Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC)

Augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) includes different ways of communicating that can supplement or support spoken language. AAC may involve unaided methods, such as gestures and signs, or aided systems, such as communication boards, picture supports, and speech-generating devices or applications.

AAC assessment and support focus on identifying options that fit the child's communication needs, abilities, environments, and communication partners. Support may include helping families and professionals select appropriate tools and integrate them into everyday interactions, activities, and routines.
Clinical Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder

I have specialized training in autism assessment, including the administration of the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule, Second Edition (ADOS-2), and the Autism Diagnostic Interview–Revised (ADI-R).

These standardized instruments contribute to a broader clinical assessment. Their findings are considered alongside developmental history, clinical observations, and other relevant information to build a comprehensive understanding of the child's profile.
The assessment process can help identify strengths and areas of need, inform clinical decision-making, and guide appropriate recommendations and next steps.
Parent Support & Education

My work with parents includes parent-mediated interventions (PMIs), parent coaching, and psychoeducation, depending on the child's needs and the family's priorities. The aim is to give parents a clearer understanding of their child and practical, evidence-informed ways to support communication, participation, and everyday functioning.
Parent-Mediated Interventions for Social Communication

I have specialized training in parent-mediated interventions that support children's social communication and interaction skills. Through parent coaching, I work with parents during everyday interactions, helping them recognize and build on their child's communication attempts and create opportunities for interaction and learning.

This may involve observing parent-child interactions, modelling strategies, guiding parents as they practise, and providing individualized feedback. Strategies may include following the child's interests, responding to communication attempts, and embedding learning opportunities into play and daily routines.
The aim is to help parents understand not only what strategies to use, but also how and when to use them with their own child.
Parent-Mediated Interventions for Challenging Behavior
I have training in parent-mediated interventions that help parents better understand and respond to challenging behavior.

The work focuses on understanding the factors that may influence behavior, recognizing patterns and triggers, adapting routines and environments, supporting communication, and teaching alternative skills. Parents are supported in developing practical, evidence-informed strategies that can be used consistently in everyday situations.
The emphasis is on understanding the function or meaning of behavior and helping children communicate, participate, and navigate everyday situations more effectively.
Psychoeducation for Parents
Psychoeducation helps parents develop a clearer understanding of their child's communication, learning, interaction, and developmental profile.

This may include discussing a child's strengths and difficulties, how they learn and interact, and the factors that may influence their participation in everyday activities. The aim is to help parents make sense of their child's needs and identify practical ways to support them at home and in other familiar environments.
ABA-Informed Support for Learning, Communication & Everyday Skills
Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) provides a framework for understanding how learning and behavior are influenced by environmental factors and everyday experiences.

My ongoing training in behavior analysis builds on my clinical experience and deepens my understanding of learning, motivation, communication, and behavior. I draw on behavior-analytic principles to support functional communication, learning, independence, and participation in everyday life.

This may include identifying meaningful learning goals, understanding factors that influence behavior, supporting the development of functional skills, and helping children participate more successfully in everyday routines.
Professional Consultation & Implementation Support
I provide consultation to educators, school teams, shadow teachers, and other professionals supporting children with communication, developmental, and learning needs.

Consultation focuses on translating individualized recommendations into practical strategies that can be integrated into a child's everyday environment. Depending on the child's needs and the team's priorities, consultation may address augmentative and alternative communication (AAC), the implementation of ABA-based strategies, and the integration of communication and learning opportunities into daily routines.
For AAC, this may involve helping teams make communication systems accessible and use them consistently during classroom activities, transitions, play, and social interactions.

For ABA-based strategies, consultation may focus on implementing agreed-upon individualized strategies that support functional communication, skill development, participation, and independence. This may include adapting routines and environments, supporting the development of alternative skills, and promoting consistency across the child's daily settings.
/how-i-work/: Parents are an important part of the process. I work alongside families, sharing observations and strategies, teaching parents how to use them in everyday interactions, and making decisions together about what feels meaningful and realistic for their child and family.

I follow the child's lead, building on their interests, strengths, and motivation. At the same time, I intentionally structure interactions and create opportunities for learning, so that communication can develop naturally while still being purposeful.

Communication is about more than what happens during a session. I focus on meaningful, functional communication that helps a child participate, connect with others, express themselves, and be more successful in their everyday life.

Every child and every family is different. I adapt support to the child's communication profile, strengths, interests, and needs, while also considering each family's priorities, routines, and what works for them.

My work is grounded in current research, clinical experience, and an understanding of each child's individual needs and context. I draw on complementary cognitive, developmental, and behavioral perspectives to understand how children learn, communicate, interact, and participate in everyday life.

Rather than relying on a single approach, I bring together principles from these different perspectives and adapt them to the child, the family, and the goals that matter in their everyday life. I continue to learn and refine my practice as new research and clinical knowledge emerge.
/for-parents/: Wondering If Your Child Needs Support?

You may have questions about your child's communication, language, interaction, or development. You may notice that they are not communicating in the way you expected, have difficulty expressing themselves, or seem to be struggling to connect or participate in everyday interactions.
An initial conversation gives us an opportunity to understand what you are noticing, answer your questions, and consider together whether an assessment or intervention would be helpful.
What Can an Assessment Tell Us?
An assessment is an opportunity to better understand your child, not simply to look for what is difficult.

It helps build a picture of their communication and language, their strengths, the areas where they may need support, and the factors that may be influencing their everyday communication. The findings can then help guide meaningful next steps.
What Does Intervention Look Like?
Intervention can involve direct work with your child, parent-mediated intervention, or a combination of both, depending on your child's needs and your family's priorities.

When working directly with your child, I use play, interaction, and everyday activities to create meaningful opportunities for communication and learning. When working through parent-mediated intervention, I work directly with you as a parent, teaching and practising strategies together. I may observe you interacting with your child, guide you as you try different strategies, and provide individualized feedback to help you use them in everyday life.

The aim is for parents to understand not only what to do, but also how and when to use strategies with their own child, so that opportunities for communication and learning can continue beyond the session.
What Is ABA-Informed Support?

Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is an approach that examines how learning and behavior are influenced by the environment and everyday experiences. It can be used to support the development of communication, learning, daily living skills, and greater independence.

My work draws on behavior-analytic principles to help understand what may influence a child's behavior, identify meaningful learning goals, and support the development of functional skills. This may include helping a child communicate their needs, participate in everyday routines, develop new skills, and find more effective ways to respond to challenging situations.
As my training in behavior analysis is still ongoing, I provide behavior-analytic support under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA).
Can We Work Online?
Yes. Online sessions can be particularly well suited to parent-mediated interventions and parent coaching.

During an online session, I can teach you strategies, observe you interacting with your child, and provide individualized feedback as you practise. This allows us to work directly with the routines and interactions that are part of your child's everyday life.
Depending on your child's needs, support can also combine online parent coaching with in-person sessions.
What Happens Next?

If you are wondering whether support could be helpful for your child, you can get in touch to discuss your concerns. We can start by understanding what you are noticing and what you would like support with, and then consider the next step together.
/contact/: If you have questions about your child's communication or development, or would like to discuss whether support could be helpful, I'd be happy to help.
You can get in touch to share what you have been noticing and what you would like support with. We can then discuss your concerns and consider the most appropriate next step together.
Sessions are offered in Arabic, French, and English, both in person and online, depending on the child's and family's needs.
